## How an engagement like this runs

Most engagements — whether an MRV pipeline, a land-use scenario, a connectivity assessment, a resilience study, or a capacity-building programme — follow the same three-phase arc, from initial scoping through to a client-ready deliverable.
:::

::: {.eg-approach-grid .eg-approach-cards}
::: {.eg-approach-item}
::: {.eg-approach-head}
[01]{.eg-approach-badge}

### Establish the reference case
:::

We start by building a defensible baseline — satellite-derived land cover, biomass, connectivity, or social-ecological indicators for the area of interest — validated against whatever field data, local knowledge, or ancillary datasets are available. This baseline is the yardstick everything else is measured against.
:::

::: {.eg-approach-item}
::: {.eg-approach-head}
[02]{.eg-approach-badge}

### Track change and model scenarios
:::

We run the monitoring, modeling, or scenario pipeline appropriate to the service — longitudinal change detection, land-use projections, corridor or resilience modeling — on a cadence that matches the client's decision timeline, not just a one-off snapshot.
:::

::: {.eg-approach-item}
::: {.eg-approach-head}
[03]{.eg-approach-badge}

### Package a client-ready deliverable
:::

Findings are documented and packaged to withstand scrutiny — whether that means a registry audit, a donor report, a county planning submission, or a workshop handoff — with the methodology reproducible and the assumptions stated plainly.
:::
:::
